checks: The anchored nonvertical capacities are continuous and attained. At t=−R a sufficiently large finite tilt exactly retains the original vertical included fibers, including the whole fibers on the vertical boundary. Thresholds outside the compact range add no new constraints.
Any uniform positive slack permits scalar multiplication. Compactness of conditional barycenters in K then gives nonempty nested limit sets.

A strict affine separator has uniformly negative expectation over all sufficiently near-tight caps. The quadratic Taylor remainder is uniform over conditional laws because K is compact. Positive slack controls all other caps, and the affine exponential tilt is log-concave on the actual affine support.
Null caps stay null under the tilt and the total mass grows strictly by the positive global affine mean. Carathéodory applies in the r-dimensional affine support, including r=0.

On positive limiting capacity the unnormalized restrictions have the exact limiting mass, remain dominated by ρ and are supported on the closed limiting cap, so they must equal the entire tight restriction. In the zero case limits of conditional probabilities are supported on suppρ and the limiting closed cap, which is an equality plane by zero target mass. The proof deliberately allows an improper equality face.

dependencies.hypotheses: A finite sampled family of compact convex fibers and a fixed target base gives exactly the continuous finite-attained directional capacity in the displayed formula.
The frozen attainment proof supplies a positive-mass optimizing log-concave measure on fixed compact K, subject to exactly the ambient closed halfspace domination constraints used here.

overlap.comparison: The capacity theorem gives the necessary compact parameter model. It has no tilt optimality or limiting conditional-barycenter conclusion.

readability: Multiplication by an affine exponential preserves log-concavity by the log-concave density characterization on the actual affine support, with the point-mass case immediate. The draft does not use the separate positive-mass contact theorem in the source.
summary: The affine tilt yields the finite asymptotically tight barycenter certificate, with the positive and zero capacity limit cases correctly distinguished.
